document.title: Politburo Session, February 26, 1987
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan and the Soviet Withdrawal 1989 20 Years Later
document.note: Gorbachev repeatedly returns to the need to withdraw Soviet troops while struggling with how to explain it, not opening discussion on who is to blame. Gromyko admits introducing troops was a mistake but notes it followed 11 requests from the Afghan government.

persons.name: Mikhail Gorbachev
persons.role: General Secretary of the CPSU; chaired the Politburo discussion on Afghanistan

mentions.quote: The material assistance to Afghanistan: expenses are huge. But they would be justified if they solved the Afghan problem.
troop withdrawal is the only correct decision. However, at the present moment, some other decisions might be needed too.

persons.name: Eduard Shevardnadze
persons.role: Soviet Foreign Minister and Politburo member

mentions.quote: Once again we made a mistake—did not foresee what was in store for us. And now withdrawing the troops is the only right solution.

persons.name: Andrei Gromyko
persons.role: Politburo member; Chairman of the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet

mentions.quote: But they asked us to introduce the troops eleven times. We kept refusing.

persons.name: Najib
persons.role: Afghan communist leader (PDPA); his chief Soviet adviser is mentioned

mentions.quote: Let us take some things from what Plyanichko (main Najib's adviser) is proposing.

events.description: Politburo session on Afghanistan: Gorbachev, Shevardnadze and Gromyko discuss material assistance and troop withdrawal.

CPSU Politburo session where Gorbachev, Shevardnadze and Gromyko discuss material assistance to Afghanistan and decide that troop withdrawal is the only correct decision, while not hurrying to pull back advisers.
Gromyko states that Afghan leaders asked the USSR to introduce troops eleven times, and that the USSR refused repeatedly.
Gorbachev says troop withdrawal is the only correct decision, rejecting sending 200 thousand more troops, and says some of Plyanichko's proposals should be adopted.

key_claims: Gorbachev says Soviet material aid to Afghanistan is hugely expensive and justified only if it solves the Afghan problem.
Shevardnadze says troop withdrawal is the only right solution.
Gromyko says Afghanistan asked the USSR eleven times to introduce troops and doubts a viable Afghan army can be built.
Gorbachev says sending 200,000 more troops would mean failure of the whole course, so withdrawal is the only correct decision.
Gorbachev urges not rushing the withdrawal of advisers lest the USSR appear to be running away.
